en: Verses on the Vast Aspiration,
composed by Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna;
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu Shi Guang [Xing].
All classes of sentient beings throughout the inexhaustible past, future, and present,
and all the vast and boundless Buddha-fields— may these be filled with the atoms of those infinite lands.
Furthermore, may each atom be a buddha-field, And vast buddha-fields as numerous as atoms;
Within each field, the Honored Ones of Perfect Enlightenment, As infinite as atoms, I universally prostrate to them all.
I shall praise every Buddha within all the buddha-fields, as numerous as atoms;
with a single-minded devotion, I shall constantly make offerings for as many vast eons as there are atoms.
I prostrate to all Buddhas and the assembly of the Dharma, and I take constant refuge in the Triple Gem.
I offer all these exquisite flowers and heaps of various jewels as constant and universal gifts.
Whatever transgressions I have already committed, I now repent of them all completely;
whatever transgressions I have not yet committed, I shall always avoid them at all times.
Whatever supreme merits there may be, I always rejoice in them all;
I dedicate this merit to sentient beings and to the fruit of the Buddha’s unsurpassed enlightenment.
As taught in the True Dharma of the Buddha, my power of aspiration is firm and true;
I shall constantly make offerings to all World-Honored Ones, and may I ultimately attain Buddhahood.
May I, in every birth, possess profound wisdom, Ever like the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; With a compassionate heart,
may I pacify suffering and save the world, Like the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara,
May I gaze upon sentient beings with eyes of noble kindness, And be no different from the Honored One Samantabhadra.
With a compassionate mind, I skillfully observe all categories of sentient beings; May I always be like the Honored One Maitreya.
In giving, may my vows be like the treasury of space; In upholding the precepts, may they be like supernatural powers and wisdom.
In patience and diligence—the two gates of practice— May I be entirely like those who are ever-diligent.
May the power of meditative concentration gather all distractions;
may I become like Vajrapāṇi, skillfully expounding the various Dharma-gates of the ten bhūmis;
may I speak of wisdom and vows like Vajragarbha, and skillfully inquire of the Buddha, the World-Honored One; and may I become like Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin.
May my profound mind and wisdom be fully steadfast; May I always possess such firm wisdom.
With unimpeded supernormal powers and skillful means, May I become like Vimalakīrti.
May I well protect the roots of goodness in all sentient beings, And with diligent vigor, may my vows be ever courageous.
May I excel in expounding the dharmas of the pāramitās and so forth;
May I become like Akṣayamati, endowed with immeasurable and wondrous voices. May I be no different from the Honored One of Wondrous Sound (Ghoṣadatta);
May I draw near to spiritual friends with a mind free from indolence. May I be, in birth after birth, like Sudhana.
The Dharma that proclaims the ineffable nature of space—may I attain such a treasury as space;

May I be like the Earth, which nurtures all worlds, And universally benefit beings like the Honored One, the Earth Treasury, Quieting poverty and suffering to aid sentient beings; May I be no different from the Deity of the Treasure Treasury.
From my speech may the inexhaustible jewels of the wondrous Dharma emerge;
May I become like Dharmodgata, with wisdom firm, sharp, and ever-diligent, And may I be no different from the Honored One Sadāprarudita.
These supreme sons of the Buddhas possess boundless and most excellent accumulations of merit;
their renown is vast and inexhaustible—may my own renown likewise be so.
This praise of the Buddha’s mass of merit is supreme, most excellent, and exceedingly vast;
may all sentient beings in the world universally dwell in that most sublime mass of merit.
Verses on the Vast Aspiration for Enlightenment (Bodhicittotpāda)
